datasets_evaluated.evidence: To perform and evaluate our proposed method, we conduct experiments on two modern DoH traffic datasets, CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 (MontazeriShatoori et al., 2020) and DoH-Tunnel-Traffic-HKD (Mitsuhashi et al., 2023).

label_source.evidence: The dataset includes implementing the DoH protocol in applications using five different browsers and tools and four servers to capture benign DoH, malicious DoH, and non-DoH traffic.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: WEDoHTool extracts the length sequence of initial TLS records with application data from several initial packets of each unidirectional flow for early identification.

model_family.evidence: Specifically, WEDoHTool filters out DoH traffic from heavy background traffic with a lightweight TextCNN and then identifies the specific DoH tools based on a Transformer encoder with the self-attention mechanism.

split_protocols.evidence: We randomly pick 80% of the samples as the training set and the remaining 20% as the testingset in each run.

metrics.evidence: We evaluate all the methods from the following aspects: Accuracy, Recall, Precision, F1-score

granularity.evidence: The flow mentioned in this paper refers to a unidirectional flow

first_n_packets.evidence: Note that n, the number of initial TLS record lengths, is set to 15 in our experiment.

cost_reported.evidence: The testing time of our WEDoHTool consists of TLS record length sequence extraction, embedding representation learning, and classifier testing.
